identity.life_stage: married to an active-duty soldier, two children under five

engagement.interaction_backstory: Third duty station in six years, third church, third set of people who do not know her yet. She found the site during a deployment and it became the one thing that did not change when the address did. She keeps a bedtime playlist that has crossed three states, and she has quietly sent it to four other spouses on post the week their husbands left.

depth.core_contradiction: The one everyone leans on at every new post, and she has not had a friend who knew her for more than twenty-six months since she was twenty-two.
depth.wound: She stopped unpacking the good dishes in 2023 and has not admitted why.
depth.longing: A church where somebody notices when she is not there.
depth.faith_journey: Church of Christ, a cappella, her grandparents' congregation; the tradition is the only continuous address she has, and she guards it more fiercely with every move.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Says 'we're good' before anyone asks; organizes everything into 'the plan'; ends hard sentences with 'so.'
depth.open_doubt: Whether God moves them or the Army does, and whether she has been calling one the other for six years.

social_graph.name: Marcus
social_graph.note: deployed; nine weeks out; they talk when they can
four women; the deepest they get is casseroles, and it is not nothing
in Alabama; wants them home; says so every call

depth.emotional_weather_default: Steady and capable; hollowed out the first two weeks after a move.
depth.daily_texture: Nap schedule taped to the fridge, the commissary run, boxes still in the garage, bedtime playlist at 7:30 sharp.
depth.sensory_anchor: Four-part harmony with no instruments, in a small hot building in Alabama, at eight years old.
depth.living_arc: Coming up on a decision about whether to stay in, and it is her decision as much as his.
